messages.author: e83d54ec65b5b8e6
messages.subject: full_join and rbind.fill
parts:
I am working with a large data set, the PISA data, with about 1.9 million records.
I need to combine stuff from different years, and for most of this work dplyr works wonderfully
and fast. 
To complete transition from plyr to dplyr, I would need the equivalent if
join( .... , type="full") or rbind.fill.
Will these be available in dplyr in the near future?

messages.author: 3afa2b67ef806635
messages.subject: Re: full_join and rbind.fill
parts:
Hi Erich,

Thanks for the tip on rbind_list and rbind_all. I only had three needs left for plyr: rbind.fill, rename and aaply.  Now I'm down to needing only two!  rename could be moved over, but aaply seems totally outside the range of dplyr's mission. Garrett Grolemund suggested I use tidyr to make the data "long", get a mean across variables (well, observations in that form) and then make it "wide" again. That works, but it blows students minds compared to aaplying the mean function across rows.

Cheers,
Bob

messages.subject: Re: full_join and rbind.fill
parts: That would be a great way to do it if we were headed towards matrix algebra. Many are SAS users who are used to using the mean function on rows. They want to enter mean(var1, var2, var3, var4) as they're used to doing, so they're happy to see that function finally do what they want when aaply does it.  -Bob

Why not teach them matrix multiplication:

> m <- matrix(1:20, 4)
> m

[1,]    1    5    9   13   17
[2,]    2    6   10   14   18
[3,]    3    7   11   15   19
[4,]    4    8   12   16   20

> m %*% c(1,1,1,1,1)
     [,1]
[1,]   45
[2,]   50
[3,]   55
[4,]   60

> m %*% c(1,1,1,1,1) / ncol(m)
     [,1]
[1,]    9
[2,]   10
[3,]   11
[4,]   12

messages.subject: Re: full_join and rbind.fill
parts:
Bob and David,

have a look at Duncan Murdoch's tables package.
tabular allows to define a function argument Percent, which, if used cleverly,
can do all sorts of rowwise computations on a table.

And getting rename over to dplyr really should be almost trivial.
It is just an operation on names of lists.

messages.subject: Re: full_join and rbind.fill
parts: aaply-ing the mean function across rows does the same thing as rowMeans (probably slower though), but I wanted to show them how to apply any function row-wise. It just occurred to me that simply transposing the data and using summarise_each might be the simplest approach to explain while avoiding plyr.  I'll have to check out the tables package too. I've never use that. Thanks for all the suggestions!  -Bob
